A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REVIS study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and support direct comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination and reasoning benchmark results, latent-state analyses, ablations, latency measurements, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of Qwen2.5-VL-32B, Qwen3-VL, and MMMU-Pro.

M1.justification: The visual and language-prior vectors, orthogonal projection, calibrated layer selection, and risk-gated steering remain unchanged. Both algorithms and the detailed procedure in Appendix G are retained; the additional backbones use the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMMU-Pro with four-option, ten-option, and vision-only evaluations, including questions whose textual context is embedded in the image (Appendices A and F.3). This introduces substantial new task and input conditions alongside the retained POPE, CHAIR, MME, and MM-Vet coverage. Extraction and calibration data remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing experiments retain the same comparators: Regular decoding, VCD, M3ID, ONLY, AGLA, and VTI, where originally evaluated. The added experiments compare REVIS with the existing Regular baseline; no new competing mitigation method is evaluated.

E3.justification: The evaluation expands beyond the original 7B/8B setting to Qwen2.5-VL-32B and adds Qwen3-VL-8B. New experiments include 64/128/512-token evaluations on these backbones and MMMU-Pro accuracy across three formats and their average. Existing experiments retain their stated protocols; explicit sizes for previously evaluated models are additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 extends generation-length sensitivity testing to Qwen2.5-VL-32B and Qwen3-VL in Tables 12 and 14. The original intensity, layer, and threshold ablations, latent-space visualizations, and case studies remain unchanged. Appendix F.5 discusses existing evidence rather than introducing a separate controlled projection-conditioning experiment.

E5.justification: Run-count, seed, and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged. The added tables contain point estimates without newly reported confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run procedures.

E6.justification: Original scores are retained, while v2 Tables 12–14 add substantial results for larger and newer backbones and MMMU-Pro. For the added 32B comparison at 512 tokens, Regular versus REVIS CHAIR_S is 52.00% versus 46.00%; MM-Vet is 74.31 versus 74.13, and MMMU-Pro average accuracy is 0.422 versus 0.435. Qwen3-VL POPE accuracy is 89.05% versus 89.48%. These are newly reported comparisons, not revisions of v1 scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, projection formula, risk score, layer-selection criterion, and steering equations are unchanged. Appendix F.5 adds an informal conditioning explanation, without a new formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the claims that training-free sparse orthogonal steering reduces hallucination while preserving reasoning and efficiency. The introduction now specifies five benchmarks and seven models, making the expanded supporting evidence explicit without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix F.5 discusses near-parallel visual and language-prior directions shrinking the projected vector and argues why the extraction construction avoids this in practice. Section 7 updates the evaluated scale from 7B/8B to include 32B, while retaining the perceptual-blindness limitation and untested 70B+ scalability.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 specifies model sizes and variants, including the Mistral-based LLaVA-NeXT checkpoint. Appendix F.3 reports that calibration selects Layer 62 for the 32B model. The existing implementation appendix, extraction sizes, hardware disclosure, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the Qwen3-VL technical report and MMMU-Pro to support the new evaluations. Section 2 and the positioning relative to existing hallucination-mitigation and activation-steering methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short scalability subsection and appendix discussion, updates setup descriptions and cross-references, clarifies model naming, and makes small wording corrections. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12–14 and relocates and renumbers the original Tables 12–13 as Tables 15–16. Figure 4 is slightly enlarged, and surrounding text and floats are reflowed. Existing figures and table designs are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The 32B evaluation partly addresses v1's explicitly acknowledged restriction to small models, while Qwen3-VL and MMMU-Pro provide additional checks of generalization and utility preservation. These strengthen the empirical support for the unchanged method. The gain is limited because the added comparisons use only Regular decoding and provide no uncertainty estimates for small, sometimes mixed performance changes.
